name: Clean supersaw: unison count, detune, blend, width
goal: Build mix-ready supersaws: simple saw frames (not complex WT sweeps), 6–12 unison voices, balanced detune/blend, optional mono sub + noise, EQ→compress→delay→reverb, light hyper/dimension, subtle warp, and global unison width/stack modes for chord phase correlation.

source.title: 5 Power Tips for Better Supersaws in Serum

prerequisites: Wavetable synth with unison detune/blend, sub/noise, FX rack, global unison width/stack

outputs.name: supersaw_patch
outputs.description: Clean wide supersaw usable in a mix

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided captions; do not invent UI or settings.
Original synthesis only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Pigments/Phase Plant/etc.) to portable osc/filter/FX roles for a browser or generic hybrid synth; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable signal-flow and motion relationships over vendor-specific preset names.
Avoid sweeping complex wavetable frames while heavily detuned — timbre becomes incoherent.
For chords, keep detune/blend more conservative than for mono drops; consider reducing unison width toward ~50% for phase correlation.

steps.action: Load a simple saw (or rounded/noisy saw variant), not a multi-frame complex WT you plan to sweep aggressively.
Set unison ~6–12 (example ~10); set detune and blend near mid — extreme detune+blend is for FX, not clean chords.
Optional Osc B: fewer unison voices, pitch ±octaves, lower level to thicken without doubling chaos.
Optional centered saw sub one octave down (no unison) for mono mid-weight; quiet unique noise sample for texture.
steps.expect: Center weight + air; still sounds like a supersaw dry

steps.action: FX order example: EQ (cut lows, lift highs) → compression → ping-pong delay → reverb last; optional light hyper/dimension detune on the bus (can widen even the sub).
Subtle warp (e.g. bend+/−) via envelope/LFO for 3D motion — keep amounts small on supersaws.
Global unison: reduce width (~50%) for better chord phase correlation; try stack modes (super, fifths, center−2, octave) sparingly; warp-offset per voice only if warp is intentional.

verification: Dry (pre-FX) still sounds like a clean supersaw
Sub (if used) remains more centered than unison voices
